programme.subtitle: AWS Migration and Transfer
programme.description: A Intermediate Follow Along for AWS Migration and Transfer.
programme.learningOutcome: Plan and perform a small database full-load migration with AWS DMS, transfer the resulting objects with AWS DataSync, and build a concrete Storage Gateway Volume Gateway cached-versus-stored configuration plan; verify each outcome and safely remove only the resources created by the lab.

phases.title: Prepare identity, tools and migration plan
phases.description: Create the training identity, CLI profile, local files and a clear service-selection model.

phases.title: Build the DMS source environment
phases.description: Create a dedicated network, secure MariaDB source, Secrets Manager credential and exact AWS DMS IAM roles.

phases.title: Run the DMS full-load migration
phases.description: Create the DMS replication infrastructure, endpoints and full-load task, then verify database rows arrive in Amazon S3.

phases.title: Transfer DMS objects with DataSync
phases.description: Create S3 DataSync locations and transfer the migrated objects to a second training bucket.

phases.title: Plan Volume Gateway configurations
phases.description: Compare cached and stored volumes, create a concrete cached-volume sizing plan and identify when each design fits.

phases.title: Review SAA-C03 migration decisions
phases.description: Distinguish DMS, DataSync and Storage Gateway by data type, transfer pattern, cutover and ongoing-access requirements.

phases.title: Reverse-dependency cleanup
phases.description: Delete DMS, DataSync, S3, EC2, IAM, Secrets Manager, networking and local resources in verified safe order.

tasks.title: Create the DMS training VPC, two subnets and security groups
tasks.goal: Create a dedicated two-AZ VPC with public routing, a source-database security group and a DMS replication security group.
tasks.whyItMatters: A DMS replication subnet group needs subnets in at least two Availability Zones, while the replication instance must be able to reach the source endpoint.

consoleSteps.title: Create the DMS training VPC, two subnets and security groups

instructions.text: Create VPC fa-migration-vpc with IPv4 CIDR 10.70.0.0/16.
Create fa-migration-public-a in eu-west-2a with CIDR 10.70.1.0/24.
Create fa-migration-public-b in eu-west-2b with CIDR 10.70.2.0/24.
Enable auto-assign public IPv4 on both training subnets.
Create internet gateway fa-migration-igw and attach it to fa-migration-vpc.
Associate both public subnets with fa-migration-public-rt.
Create fa-migration-dms-sg in fa-migration-vpc with no inbound rules and default outbound allowed.
Add inbound MySQL/Aurora TCP 3306 to fa-migration-source-db-sg with source fa-migration-dms-sg.
Do not add SSH or internet-wide MySQL access.

tasks.title: Launch and seed the self-managed MariaDB source without exposing its password
tasks.goal: Launch one Amazon Linux 2023 source instance, generate a Secrets Manager credential and seed three rows through Systems Manager.
tasks.whyItMatters: The source database demonstrates a real database endpoint while the credential remains generated and stored in Secrets Manager rather than in the manuscript.

consoleSteps.title: Launch and seed the self-managed MariaDB source without exposing its password

instructions.text: Launch one Amazon Linux 2023 instance named fa-migration-mysql-source.
Do not create or select a key pair.
Under Advanced details paste source-user-data.sh from Task 3.
Wait for EC2 status checks to pass and for the instance to appear in Systems Manager Managed nodes.
Create Other type of secret named fa-migration/mysql-source.
The CLI route below shows how to generate an alphanumeric runtime password and store username, password, port and host without printing the password.
After the secret exists, use Systems Manager Run Command with configure-source.sh to create migrationdb.customers and three harmless rows.
Do not display the secret value in the console after creation.

dnf install -y mariadb105-server
systemctl enable mariadb

tasks.title: Verify the migrated objects and compare full load with CDC
tasks.goal: Prove the three training rows reached S3 and explain when a production database migration would add CDC and Multi-AZ.
tasks.whyItMatters: A successful task is not enough; migration planning includes validating migrated data and deciding how to handle changes made during the migration window.

Review the planning distinction: this lab uses full load because the source is static after seeding.

For long-running/ongoing replication, consider Multi-AZ for the DMS replication instance.

tasks.title: Review the SAA-C03 migration and transfer decision points
tasks.goal: Turn the three service exercises into clear selection rules for database migration, data movement and hybrid storage.
tasks.whyItMatters: The exam commonly tests which migration service matches the data type and whether the requirement is one-time transfer, ongoing replication or ongoing hybrid access.

consoleSteps.title: Review the SAA-C03 migration and transfer decision points
consoleSteps.instruction: AWS DMS: choose it for database migration and replication between supported database endpoints.

instructions.text: AWS DMS: choose it for database migration and replication between supported database endpoints.
DMS full load: moves the existing source data once.
DMS full load plus CDC: use it when source changes continue during migration and low-downtime cutover is required.
DMS replication instance: provides the compute that connects to source/target endpoints and performs replication work.
DMS endpoints: define connection details; this lab uses Secrets Manager for source authentication.
DataSync: choose it for managed high-speed transfer of files/objects between supported storage systems and AWS storage.
DataSync locations define source and destination; a DataSync task defines how the transfer runs.
DataSync is not a transactional database CDC engine.
Volume Gateway: choose it when applications need ongoing iSCSI block-storage access integrated with AWS, rather than a one-time copy.
Cached Volume Gateway: primary data lives in Amazon S3 and frequently accessed data is cached locally.
Stored Volume Gateway: primary data remains local and is asynchronously backed up to AWS.
Stored Volume Gateway cannot be deployed on Amazon EC2.
Exam trigger: migrate a live relational database with minimal downtime -> DMS with CDC where supported.
Exam trigger: move large file/object datasets to AWS repeatedly or on schedule -> DataSync.
Exam trigger: keep existing block-storage applications using iSCSI while integrating storage with AWS -> Volume Gateway.
Exam trap: Storage Gateway provides ongoing hybrid access; it is not simply a faster substitute for DataSync.

warnings.safety: Delete only exact fa-migration resources and the two exact DMS service roles created by this lab. Do not delete a DMS role if it existed before the lab or is used by unrelated DMS workloads.
warnings.credentials: Never create root access keys and never place the MariaDB password, AWS access key or secret key in the manuscript, local scripts, screenshots or Study Tracker. The database password is generated at runtime and stored in Secrets Manager.
warnings.region: Every cloud resource in the active lab is created in eu-west-2. The two DMS subnets use eu-west-2a and eu-west-2b.

steps.title: Remove DMS full-load task
steps.instruction:
Console:
- Stop it if necessary, then delete the DMS task. Exact target: fa-migration-full-load.
CLI:

- aws datasync delete-location --location-arn $DS_SOURCE_ARN --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws datasync delete-location --location-arn $DS_DEST_ARN --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin

- aws dms delete-endpoint --endpoint-arn $TARGET_ENDPOINT_ARN --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws dms delete-replication-instance --replication-instance-arn $REPL_ARN --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws dms wait replication-instance-deleted --filters Name=replication-instance-id,Values=fa-migration-replication --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws dms delete-replication-subnet-group --replication-subnet-group-identifier fa-migration-dms-subnets --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws s3 rm "s3://$ARCHIVE_BUCKET" --recursive --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws s3api delete-bucket --bucket $ARCHIVE_BUCKET --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws s3 rm "s3://$DMS_BUCKET" --recursive --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws s3api delete-bucket --bucket $DMS_BUCKET --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws ec2 terminate-instances --instance-ids $SOURCE_INSTANCE_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws ec2 wait instance-terminated --instance-ids $SOURCE_INSTANCE_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws secretsmanager delete-secret --secret-id fa-migration/mysql-source --force-delete-without-recovery --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- $SOURCE_SG_ID = aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=group-name,Values=fa-migration-source-db-sg --query "SecurityGroups[0].GroupId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin; $DMS_SG_ID = aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=group-name,Values=fa-migration-dms-sg --query "SecurityGroups[0].GroupId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws ec2 delete-security-group --group-id $SOURCE_SG_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws ec2 delete-security-group --group-id $DMS_SG_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- $VPC_ID = aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-migration-vpc --query "Vpcs[0].VpcId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin; $RT_ID = aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-migration-public-rt --query "RouteTables[0].RouteTableId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin; $IGW_ID = aws ec2 describe-internet-gateways --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-migration-igw --query "InternetGateways[0].InternetGatewayId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- $ASSOC_IDS = aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids $RT_ID --query "RouteTables[0].Associations[?Main==`false`].RouteTableAssociationId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- foreach ($A in ($ASSOC_IDS -split "\s+")) { if ($A) { aws ec2 disassociate-route-table --association-id $A --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin } }
- aws ec2 delete-route-table --route-table-id $RT_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws ec2 detach-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id $IGW_ID --vpc-id $VPC_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws ec2 delete-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id $IGW_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- $SUBNET_A_ID = aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-migration-public-a --query "Subnets[0].SubnetId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin; $SUBNET_B_ID = aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-migration-public-b --query "Subnets[0].SubnetId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id $SUBNET_A_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws ec2 delete-subnet --subnet-id $SUBNET_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
- aws ec2 delete-vpc --vpc-id $VPC_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-migration-admin
